rules.text: If the percentage inscriptions inside the pie slices are valid, comparable market-share values for the named Europe smartphone categories, then the category with the largest printed percentage is the displayed market-share leader; if the task reserves the premium retail promotion budget for that leader, the matching brand option is supported.
rules.component: pie-slice label decoding and task-to-action relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if the pie labels correctly encode comparable Europe market shares and the dashboard values are the intended current evidence source.

rules.text: If a task requires a current market-share leader, a chart supports that temporal qualification only when its displayed scope or the supplied task context establishes that the shown values are current; absence of a visible date or current-period label leaves independent temporal verification incomplete.
rules.conditions: Applies to whether the chart itself visibly establishes the required current-period status, not to the relative ordering of its printed percentages.

observations.location: entire visible chart area, including title and pie labels

chains.claim: The chart visibly supports a displayed percentage ordering but does not independently show a reporting date or current-period label. added_observations.content: The Apple-labeled sector visibly occupies a larger portion of the pie than each of the Xiaomi-, Samsung-, and Others-labeled sectors.
The Apple sector extends from the top radial boundary around the right side to the lower-right boundary, while the other labeled sectors occupy smaller portions on the left side.

refinements.reason: The base chain uses the printed percentage inscriptions; these visible sector extents independently corroborate that the Apple-associated sector is the largest displayed sector.

question_responses.reason: The added observations provide the requested visible geometric cross-check without replacing the base chain's percentage-label decoding.
